title: Unhindered (Acts 28:17–31)
hook: Acts ends with Paul in Rome under guard, welcoming all, preaching without hindrance
tomorrow: a church splits into fan clubs. whose club does Paul go after first?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Malta: a fire in the rain and strangers taking in strangers. The line: no little kindness.

Some endings feel unfinished: a show canceled mid-season, a friend who moves before you said the thing. Acts ends a little like that. Paul reaches Rome at last, and he isn't in a cell. He "was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him." A place of his own, a guard at the door, and a chain. Visitors can come in. He can't go out. Then a few scenes, and the book stops.
screen: `ENDINGS THAT FEEL UNFINISHED.` → `ROME, AT LAST.` → `A GUARD, A CHAIN, A ROOM.`

segments.voice: He calls together the leaders of the Jewish community in Rome and tells them why he's bound: "for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain." They've heard nothing against him, they say, and they want to hear him out. So they come to his lodging, and from morning till evening he talks. Acts reports the result plainly: "And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not." Then the last verses of the book: "And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him, Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him." No trial scene. No verdict from Caesar. Acts doesn't say what happened next. It stops in an open room: the chain still on, the guard still there, and everyone who comes let in. For a week when you can't change much, that's what this ending hands you. Not freedom from the chain. A door you choose to keep open.
screen: `THE HOPE OF ISRAEL.` · `SOME BELIEVED, SOME NOT.` · `RECEIVED ALL THAT CAME.` · `THE BOOK STOPS IN AN OPEN ROOM.` · then, large: `NO MAN FORBIDDING HIM.`

segments.voice: Pick up your phone and find one name you haven't heard from in a while, someone you'd be glad to see at your door. Send one plain line that leaves the door open, with nothing asked back. Then set the phone face down and rest.
Unhindered. How Acts ends: a prisoner in a hired house, a chain on his wrist, welcoming all, and no one stopping him.
Keep this one: no man forbidding him, chain still on and door still open. That's the book of Acts.

howItsDone: Some churches read from Acts in the weeks after Easter, and readers who go straight through notice that the book ends without telling how Paul's trial turned out.

original.note: Greek: unhindered, without hindrance. The King James gives it as no man forbidding him.

chat.says: dad says GO to chicago. he made a whole speech. i still feel like i'm leaving everyone mid-storm.
options: Go, and keep your door open: call home at night, and let them reach you anytime.
Stay. Leaving while your dad's hurt means picking yourself over your family.
Go, and don't call much. A clean break; checking in just makes everyone sadder.
chat.meaning: Paul couldn't leave his house or lose the chain, but he received all who came. Where you are matters less than whether the door stays open.
